title: 기분을 말할 때: 속이 타요, 간 떨어질 뻔했어요
objective: By the end, you can read a short message or conversation with an emotion idiom and tell how the speaker really feels (happy, worried, relieved, shocked, angry, guilty, sad or embarrassed).
summary: This worksheet teaches ten common Korean idioms for feelings and how to work out the real feeling behind them in everyday talk.
note: These idioms are everyday spoken expressions; friends use them freely, but use them carefully with people you must be formal with.

task.title: Find the real feeling
task.line: Read each situation or message, then choose, fill in, or explain the feeling behind the idiom.

items.text: You are excited or a little nervous about something coming soon.

items.gloss: feel on top of the world
items.text: You are so happy and light that you could fly.
items.example: 드디어 비자가 나와서 날아갈 것 같아요.

items.text: A problem or a stuffy feeling is finally gone.
items.example: 오래된 짐을 다 버리니까 속이 시원하네요.

items.text: You are anxious while you wait and can do nothing.
items.example: 밤 11시인데 아이가 아직 안 들어와서 속이 타요.

items.gloss: nearly jump out of your skin
items.text: Something suddenly scared you; it is usually said in the past.
items.example: 뒤에서 갑자기 부르니까 간 떨어질 뻔했잖아.

items.text: Something is so wrong or unfair that you cannot believe it.
items.example: 만 원짜리를 오만 원에 팔다니, 기가 막혀요.

items.text: Your anger goes up to the top of your head.
items.example: 약속을 세 번이나 어겨서 화가 머리끝까지 났어요.

items.text: You feel sorry or guilty, or you worry about a duty.
items.example: 친구 결혼식에 못 가서 마음이 무거워요.

items.text: You feel deep sadness or pity, not body pain.

items.gloss: want the ground to swallow you
items.text: You are so embarrassed that you want to hide, even in a mouse hole.
items.example: 발표 중에 사장님 이름을 틀려서 쥐구멍에라도 들어가고 싶었어요.

sections.heading: Reading tip: Korean feelings live in the body
paragraphs: Korean often puts feelings in 속 (the inside, stomach), 가슴 (chest), 간 (liver) and 머리 (head). English often uses only 'heart'. So read the body word as a feeling word: 속이 타다 is worry, not stomach pain, and 가슴이 아프다 is sadness, not a chest problem.

Watch the context. 기가 막히다 is usually negative, but 기가 막히게 맛있어요 means 'amazingly delicious'. These idioms are common in speech and messages; in formal writing, plain words like 걱정되다 or 화가 나다 are safer.

sections.heading: In a real conversation
paragraphs:
가: 결과 나왔어?
나: 응, 방금 문자 왔어. 합격이래!
가: 와, 축하해! 일주일 동안 속이 탔지?
나: 응, 이제 속이 다 시원해.
Notice the change: 속이 탔다 (worried while waiting) becomes 속이 시원하다 (relieved) after the good news.

exercises: Choose the idiom that fits: 버스에서 미끄러져 넘어졌는데 사람들이 다 쳐다봤어요. 너무 창피해서 (쥐구멍에라도 들어가고 싶었어요 / 속이 시원했어요).
Read the message and answer in English. How does Minsu feel, and why?: 민수: 면접 본 지 일주일인데 아직 연락이 없어. 속이 타 죽겠어.
Fill in the blank with one word from the idiom list: 룸메이트가 말도 없이 내 케이크를 다 먹었어. 화가 ____까지 났어.
Choose the best idiom for each situation (속이 시원하다 / 간 떨어질 뻔하다 / 가슴이 뛰다): ① 10년 동안 참은 말을 드디어 다 했어요. ② 불을 끈 방에서 고양이가 갑자기 뛰어나왔어요. ③ 다음 주에 좋아하는 가수의 콘서트에 가요.
Read and answer in English. Who feels guilty, and who is shocked in a bad way?: 수진: 어제 동생한테 심한 말을 해서 마음이 무거워. / 지호: 나는 동생이 내 노트북을 떨어뜨려서 정말 기가 막혔어.
True or False: ① 장학금을 받게 돼서 날아갈 것 같아요. → The speaker is very happy. ② 길에서 다친 강아지를 보니까 가슴이 아팠어요. → The speaker had pain in the chest.
answers: He is very worried and nervous because he has not heard the result of his job interview for a week.
① 속이 시원하다 ② 간 떨어질 뻔하다 ③ 가슴이 뛰다
수진 feels guilty (마음이 무겁다). 지호 is shocked and speechless (기가 막히다).
① True ② False (the speaker felt sad and sorry for the dog)
